definition: מֹ֫לֶךְ proper name, of a divinity Molech ( ᵐ5 Μολοχ , ᵑ9 Moloch ) (= מֶלֶךְ i.e. ( divine ) King , with vowels of בּשֶׁת to denote abhorrence, Hoffm ZAW iii. 1883, 124 RS Semitic i. 353; 2nd ed. 372 ; compare Hoffm GG Abh. xxxvi. 1890 a (May, 1889), 25 ; Phoenician proper name, of divinity מלך Milk , in proper names compare Bloch , Dr Dt.222 f. ); — with article ׳ הַמּ : — the god to whom Israel sacrificed children with fire (in valley of Hinnom); ׳ העביר בָּנֵשׁ לַ מּ 2Kgs 23:10 ׳ העביר לַמּ Jer 32:35 (|| הַבַּעַל ), Lev 18:21 ( H ); ׳ נתן לַמּ Lev 20:2 ; Lev 20:3 ; Lev 20:4 ( H ); more generally ׳ לִזְנוֺת אַחֲרֵי הַמּ v Lev 20:5 ( H ). In 1Kgs 11:7 read probably מִלְכֹּם , q. v.
